result:
The proposed answer is not correct, because it ignores the fact that the projection is no longer linearly normal.

A general projection C_q ⊂ P^{d-2} is isomorphic to C and has degree d. However, the degree d line bundle has h⁰ = d, so C_q is cut out by only a hyperplane's worth of sections (d−1 of them). It is therefore not linearly normal. The syzygy index of the elliptic normal curve (d−3) does not carry over to the projection, since the index depends on the embedding and not only on the line bundle.

A check at d = 5 shows the failure. Here C_q is a quintic elliptic curve in P³. We have h⁰(O_{P³}(2)) = 10 and h⁰(O_C(2)) = 10, and C_q lies on no quadric. Its ideal is therefore not generated by quadrics, so even N_{2,1} fails and the index is 0. The formula d−3 would give 2 here, which is wrong. The value 0 is consistent with d−5, which is the value I recall from the literature, though I have not derived it for general d.

VERDICT: REJECT
